title.value: SoundChoice: Grapheme-to-Phoneme Models with Semantic Disambiguation
title.justification: The title clearly describes the focus of the paper on grapheme-to-phoneme conversion with an added emphasis on semantic disambiguation.
title.quote: SoundChoice: Grapheme-to-Phoneme Models with Semantic Disambiguation

extractions.description: The paper introduces SoundChoice, a novel Grapheme-to-Phoneme (G2P) model that operates at a sentence level to improve homograph disambiguation in speech synthesis. Leveraging a weighted homograph loss and curriculum learning that transitions from word-level to sentence-level processing, SoundChoice integrates BERT word embeddings and speech recognition techniques like multi-task learning with Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC). This results in a phoneme error rate (PER) of 2.65% and a 94% homograph accuracy on datasets including LibriSpeech and Wikipedia Homograph.
